sections.markdown:
## C2 — Warning signs, confusables and KG hints, traffic signs

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A04
A Road Turns Left sign warns of a sharp turn or curve to the left, while a Road Curves Ahead sign warns of a sharp curve left and then right. [A04]
Why it matters: group warning signs; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec10-F03 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A04
A Winding Curve Ahead sign with a speed plaque tells you to limit your speed, in the handbook example to 35 mph. [A04]
Why it matters: group warning signs; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec10-R01 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A04
A sign marked RR warns that a railroad crossing is ahead. [A04]
Why it matters: group warning signs; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec10-F06, sec10-F35 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A04
Watch for Bicyclists and Watch for Pedestrians signs mean those road users may be nearby, so drive carefully. [A04]
Why it matters: group warning signs; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec10-F12 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A04
An Obstacle in Roadway sign means a traffic island or obstruction is ahead and you may pass on either side. [A04]
Why it matters: group warning signs; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec10-F30 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A04
A Maximum Height sign gives the clearance under a bridge or structure, such as 12 feet 6 inches. [A04]
Why it matters: group warning signs; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables none [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A04
An Exit 25 mph sign means you should take the exit at no more than 25 mph. [A04]
Why it matters: group warning signs; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec10-F19 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A04
The yellow No Passing Zone pennant sits on the left side of the road and warns that passing would be hazardous. [A04]
Why it matters: group no passing; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec10-F04, sec10-F29 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A04
An Intersection Ahead sign warns of a crossing road, while a Side Road Ahead sign warns of a road joining from the right. [A04]
Why it matters: group warning signs; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables none [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A04
Roundabout Ahead, Stop Ahead and Yield Ahead signs warn that a roundabout, a stop sign or a yield sign is coming up. [A04]
Why it matters: group advance warning; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec10-F25, sec10-F26 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A04
The orange Road Work Ahead sign means crews are working in the area, so drive with care. [A04]
Why it matters: group work zones; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec10-F10 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A04
A Merging Traffic sign means traffic will merge from the right. [A04]
Why it matters: group lane changes; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec10-R14, sec10-R18 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A04
A Lane Ends Merge Left sign means the right lane is ending, so merge left and yield to traffic already in the left lane. [A04]
Why it matters: group lane changes; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec10-R12, sec10-R18 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A04
A Divided Highway Ends sign means the divided road becomes two lanes of traffic, and a Two-Way Traffic sign means two-way traffic begins, so keep right. [A04]
Why it matters: group lane changes; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables none [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A04
A Hill sign warns of a steep downgrade; every vehicle, especially a large truck, should check its brakes and gear down if needed. [A04]
Why it matters: group warning signs; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables none [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A04
Slippery When Wet warns that the road surface becomes slick in bad weather. [A04]
Why it matters: group warning signs; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec10-F17 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A04
A Right Lane Ends sign gives notice that the right lane ends in 500 feet, so prepare to merge left. [A04]
Why it matters: group lane changes; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec10-R13 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R18 | anchor: A04
A Bicyclists and Pedestrians sign marks a nearby shared crossing for both groups. [A04]
Why it matters: group warning signs; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec10-R04 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R19 | anchor: A04
Pavement markings are white or yellow, and they warn, regulate and inform drivers. [A04]
Why it matters: group pavement markings; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables none [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R20 | anchor: A04
White lines divide lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and broken white lines separate lanes on roads with more than one lane moving the same way. [A04]
Why it matters: group pavement markings; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables none [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R21 | anchor: A04
Never straddle a broken white line or cross a double yellow line. [A04]
Why it matters: group pavement markings; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables none [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R22 | anchor: A01
The pennant shape is tied to no-passing zones, while the diamond is the general warning shape. [A01]
Why it matters: group sign shapes; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec10-F03, sec10-F04 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-R23 | anchor: A01
Two different shapes, the round sign and the crossbuck, both stand for a railroad crossing, so either one means look for trains. [A01]
Why it matters: group sign shapes; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec10-F06 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-R24 | anchor: A02
Yellow is the general caution color, but orange is caution reserved for construction or maintenance, and fluorescent pink is for incidents and unplanned events. [A02]
Why it matters: group sign colors; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec10-F10, sec10-F12 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-R25 | anchor: A02
Blue signs mean services, green signs mean directions, and brown signs mean recreation or culture. [A02]
Why it matters: group sign colors; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec10-F09, sec10-F13 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-R26 | anchor: A03
Do Not Pass and Pass With Care work as a pair: the first forbids passing, and the second, posted on the right after it, ends the no-passing zone. [A03]
Why it matters: group no passing; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec10-F29 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-R27 | anchor: A03
Wrong Way means you are already in an oncoming lane, while Do Not Enter forbids going into the area in the first place. [A03]
Why it matters: group prohibitions; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec10-F31, sec10-F33 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]
